scope: S03-T02B user cancellation and page commit barrier

environment.broker: RabbitMQ 4.1 disposable test vhost and Compose worker

product_failures: collection cancellation handler did not exist for three cancellation boundary cases
a stale fencing token rejected the database commit but left the uploaded object orphaned
red.fixture_failure: the first HTTP cancellation fixture used an insufficient activation budget; it was corrected before implementation

green.dependency_audit: no known Python vulnerabilities; production frontend audit 0
green.contract: FastAPI OpenAPI snapshot and UmiOpenAPI generated client unchanged and current
green.browser: 3 Chromium tests passed after the synthetic owner was initialized correctly
green.compose: 0019 migration, real prefork job attempts=1, backend replacement proxy=401, graceful worker/scheduler exit=0 and backend exit=143 without SIGKILL

assertions.queued_http_cancel: job and collection run cancelled atomically with partial/user_cancelled
assertions.old_lease: could not complete, fail, reschedule or reclaim the cancelled job
assertions.stale_fencing_upload: rejected object was removed instead of becoming an untracked orphan

backup_restore_regression.cleanup: restore database, dump, manifest and source fixture removed

limitations: No external platform request, account session, real user content or existing MinIO instance was used.
The in-memory store proves the EvidenceStore compensation protocol, not the selected MinIO deployment's TLS, delete permission, versioning or object-lock behavior.
Cancellation stops persistence after a bounded source request returns; this slice does not add transport-level interruption of an in-flight HTTP call.
Comment and reply continuation pages, multiple roots and seven-day observation remain outside this slice.
This evidence advances but does not complete EV-007-005 or TASK-007-S03-T02.
